inputs.abstract:
A formalisation of the semi-invertible multiplicative ergodic theorem for strongly measurable,
forward-integrable cocycles $\mathcal L$ of bounded operators on a separable Banach space $X$,
over an invertible ergodic transformation of a Lebesgue probability space. No invertibility or
injectivity of the operators $\mathcal L_\omega$ is assumed.

The Lyapunov exponents are defined through the growth rates $\chi_k$ of the Bernstein numbers of
the iterates $\mathcal L^{(n)}_\omega$, and the distinct exponents $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdots$
are read off from them. The main result is the Oseledets decomposition: for each $l$ the space
splits almost surely as $X = E_1(\omega) \oplus \cdots \oplus E_{l-1}(\omega) \oplus V_l(\omega)$
into equivariant, measurable, finite-dimensional fast spaces $E_i(\omega)$, on which the cocycle
grows at rate exactly $\lambda_i$ both in norm and in slowest growth, and an invariant slow space
$V_l(\omega) = \{x : \lambda_\omega(x) \le \lambda_l\}$, with strongly measurable, tempered
projections. The decomposition is nontrivial exactly when the cocycle is quasicompact.

The submission also proves that the decomposition is unique, that the sum of the first $i$ fast
spaces is exactly the set of vectors admitting a backward history decaying at rate $\lambda_i$,
and that the Bernstein index $\nu = \lim_k \chi_k$ is the index of compactness: the growth rate of
the distance of $\mathcal L^{(n)}_\omega$ to the compact operators exists almost surely and equals
$\nu$, so that quasicompactness can be read off from that growth rate. The proofs include a version of Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem for
balanced time intervals, and Birkhoff's ergodic theorem. Several
corrections to the published paper are recorded in the errata in the source repository.

concepts.title: Auerbach's lemma
concepts.description:
Let $E$ be a real normed space of finite dimension $k$. Then there are unit vectors
$e_1, \ldots, e_k \in E$ such that
$$\max_i |a_i| \le \Bigl\| \sum_i a_i e_i \Bigr\| \quad \text{for every } a \in \mathbb{R}^k.$$
Consequently, for every real normed space $X$ and every subspace $W \le X$ of finite dimension
$m$, there is a bounded projection $P : X \to X$ onto $W$ with $\|P\| \le m$. The first statement
is Auerbach's lemma (see Wojtaszczyk 1991, II.E.11).

import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

/-!
---
title: Auerbach's lemma
type: theorem
---
Let $E$ be a real normed space of finite dimension $k$. Then there are unit vectors
$e_1, \ldots, e_k \in E$ such that
$$\max_i |a_i| \le \Bigl\| \sum_i a_i e_i \Bigr\| \quad \text{for every } a \in \mathbb{R}^k.$$
Consequently, for every real normed space $X$ and every subspace $W \le X$ of finite dimension
$m$, there is a bounded projection $P : X \to X$ onto $W$ with $\|P\| \le m$. The first statement
is Auerbach's lemma (see Wojtaszczyk 1991, II.E.11).
-/

namespace Lax606786.AuerbachLemma

/-- An Auerbach basis: unit vectors whose coefficients are controlled by the norm of the sum
(`‖a‖` is the supremum norm on `Fin k → ℝ`). -/
axiom exists_auerbach_basis {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {k : ℕ} (hk : Module.finrank ℝ E = k) :
    ∃ e : Fin k → E, (∀ i, ‖e i‖ = 1) ∧ ∀ a : Fin k → ℝ, ‖a‖ ≤ ‖∑ i, a i • e i‖

/-- A projection of norm at most `m` onto an `m`-dimensional subspace. -/
axiom exists_proj_norm_le {X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]
    (W : Submodule ℝ X) [FiniteDimensional ℝ W] {m : ℕ} (hm : Module.finrank ℝ W = m) :
    ∃ P : X →L[ℝ] X, (∀ x, P x ∈ W) ∧ (∀ w ∈ W, P w = w) ∧ ‖P‖ ≤ m

end Lax606786.AuerbachLemma

concepts.title: Backward characterisation of the fast spaces
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$, let
$(L, (\lambda_i), (m_i), (E_i), (V_l), (\Pi_l))$ be an Oseledets decomposition of $\mathcal{L}$,
and let $B_c(\omega)$ be the set of vectors with a backward history at $\omega$ decaying at
rate $c$. Then for every $i < L$ and almost every $\omega$,
$$E_1(\omega) \oplus \cdots \oplus E_i(\omega) = B_{\lambda_i}(\omega).$$
For quasicompact cocycles with a $\mu$-continuous generator ($\omega \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\omega$
norm-continuous on each piece of a countable Borel partition of $\Omega$), Froyland, Lloyd and
Quas (2013, Lemma 20) show that a full orbit lying in the fast spaces $E_i$ decays backwards at
rate $\lambda_i$, and one lying in the slow spaces $V_i$ decays no faster than rate
$\lambda_i$.

open MeasureTheory Filter TopologicalSpace

/-- The sum of the first `i` fast spaces is the set of vectors with a backward history
decaying at rate `λ_i`. -/
axiom fastSum_eq_backwardSet {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
    [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X]
    (R : Cocycle Ω X) [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X]
    {L : ℕ∞} {lam : ℕ → EReal} {m : ℕ → ℕ+}
    {E : ∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → (i : ℕ∞) < L → Ω → GrassmannianFin X (m i)}
    {V : ℕ → Ω → Submodule ℝ X} {P : ℕ → Ω → X →L[ℝ] X}
    (h : IsOseledetsDecomposition R L lam m E V P)
    (i : ℕ) (hi₁ : 1 ≤ i) (hi₂ : (i : ℕ∞) < L) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), (fastSum E i ω : Set X) = backwardSet R ω (lam i)

end Lax606786.BackwardCharacterisation

concepts.title: Backward growth from forward growth
concepts.description:
Let $\tau$ be an ergodic measure-preserving map of a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$.

- (Returns at positive density.) If $\mu(G) > 0$ and $\eta > 0$, then for almost every $\omega$ and
  all large $n$ there is $k \in [n, (1+\eta)n]$ with $\tau^k\omega \in G$.
- (The density argument.) Let $a_n : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ be measurable, $\varphi \ge 0$
  measurable and integrable, and $c \in \mathbb{R}$. Suppose that almost surely, along the orbit of
  $\omega$,
  $$a_k(\tau^k\omega) \le a_n(\tau^n\omega)\, \exp \sum_{n < t \le k} \varphi(\tau^t\omega)
    \qquad (n \le k),$$
  and that for almost every $\zeta$ and every $b < c$, $a_n(\zeta) \ge e^{bn}$ for all large $n$.
  Then for almost every $\omega$ and every $b < c$, $a_n(\tau^n\omega) \ge e^{bn}$ for all large
  $n$.

Applied with $\tau = \sigma^{-1}$ to the growth of a cocycle, the second statement turns forward
lower bounds into backward ones without any integrability of the inverse. It is the argument of
Mañé's lemma on tempered functions (Mañé 1983; González-Tokman and Quas 2015, Lemma 15).

import Mathlib.Dynamics.Ergodic.Ergodic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L1Space.Integrable
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Exp

/-!
---
title: Backward growth from forward growth
type: theorem
---
Let $\tau$ be an ergodic measure-preserving map of a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$.

- (Returns at positive density.) If $\mu(G) > 0$ and $\eta > 0$, then for almost every $\omega$ and
  all large $n$ there is $k \in [n, (1+\eta)n]$ with $\tau^k\omega \in G$.
- (The density argument.) Let $a_n : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ be measurable, $\varphi \ge 0$
  measurable and integrable, and $c \in \mathbb{R}$. Suppose that almost surely, along the orbit of
  $\omega$,
  $$a_k(\tau^k\omega) \le a_n(\tau^n\omega)\, \exp \sum_{n < t \le k} \varphi(\tau^t\omega)
    \qquad (n \le k),$$
  and that for almost every $\zeta$ and every $b < c$, $a_n(\zeta) \ge e^{bn}$ for all large $n$.
  Then for almost every $\omega$ and every $b < c$, $a_n(\tau^n\omega) \ge e^{bn}$ for all large
  $n$.

Applied with $\tau = \sigma^{-1}$ to the growth of a cocycle, the second statement turns forward
lower bounds into backward ones without any integrability of the inverse. It is the argument of
Mañé's lemma on tempered functions (Mañé 1983; González-Tokman and Quas 2015, Lemma 15).
-/

namespace Lax606786.BackwardGrowthFromForward

open MeasureTheory Filter

variable {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}

/-- Almost every orbit visits `G` in every window `[n, (1 + η) n]` with `n` large. -/
axiom ae_eventually_exists_mem_window [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {τ : Ω → Ω} (hτ : Ergodic τ μ) {G : Set Ω}
    (hG : MeasurableSet G) (hGpos : μ G ≠ 0) {η : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ k : ℕ, n ≤ k ∧ (k : ℝ) ≤ (1 + η) * n ∧ τ^[k] ω ∈ G

/-- Forward exponential lower bounds transfer along the orbit. -/
axiom ae_eventually_exp_le_backward [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {τ : Ω → Ω} (hτ : Ergodic τ μ) (a : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (ha : ∀ n, Measurable (a n)) {φ : Ω → ℝ} (hφm : Measurable φ) (hφ : Integrable φ μ)
    (hφ0 : ∀ ω, 0 ≤ φ ω) {c : ℝ}
    (hwin : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ n k : ℕ, n ≤ k →
      a k (τ^[k] ω) ≤ a n (τ^[n] ω) * Real.exp (∑ t ∈ Finset.Ioc n k, φ (τ^[t] ω)))
    (hfwd : ∀ᵐ ζ ∂μ, ∀ b : ℝ, b < c → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Real.exp (b * n) ≤ a n ζ) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ b : ℝ, b < c → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Real.exp (b * n) ≤ a n (τ^[n] ω)

end Lax606786.BackwardGrowthFromForward

  Ergodic τ μ →
    ∀ {G : Set Ω},

concepts.title: Backward growth rates of the Oseledets spaces
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$ over an invertible ergodic base
$(\Omega, \sigma, \mu)$, and $(L, \lambda, m, E, V, \Pi)$ an Oseledets decomposition of it.
Write $\zeta_n = \sigma^{-n}\omega$, so that $\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\zeta_n}$ carries the fibre
over $\zeta_n$ forward to the fibre over $\omega$. Then for almost every $\omega$:

1. (*fast spaces, from below*) for $i < L$ and every real $a < \lambda_i$, eventually
   $$g\big(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\zeta_n}, E_i(\zeta_n)\big) \ge e^{an};$$
2. (*the whole space, from above*) for every real $b > \lambda_1$, eventually
   $\|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\zeta_n}\| \le e^{bn}$;
3. (*slow spaces, from above*) for $2 \le l \le L$ and every real $b > \lambda_l$, eventually
   $\|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\zeta_n} v\| \le e^{bn}\|v\|$ for all $v \in V_l(\zeta_n)$.

These are the backward counterparts of the forward growth rates in the decomposition: the
forward statements hold at a fixed base point as $n \to \infty$, whereas here the base point
$\sigma^{-n}\omega$ moves with $n$.

In Lean, $\sigma^{-n}\omega$ is `(R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω`.

/-- Backward lower growth on the fast spaces. -/
axiom backward_growth_fastSpace [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X]
    {R : Cocycle Ω X} {L : ℕ∞} {lam : ℕ → EReal}
    {m : ℕ → ℕ+} {E : ∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → (i : ℕ∞) < L → Ω → GrassmannianFin X (m i)}
    {V : ℕ → Ω → Submodule ℝ X} {P : ℕ → Ω → X →L[ℝ] X}
    (h : IsOseledetsDecomposition R L lam m E V P)
    {i : ℕ} (hi₁ : 1 ≤ i) (hi₂ : (i : ℕ∞) < L) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), ∀ a : ℝ, (a : EReal) < lam i → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      Real.exp (a * n) ≤ growth (R.iterate n ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω))
        ((E i hi₁ hi₂ ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω)).1 : Submodule ℝ X)

/-- Backward upper growth of the whole cocycle, at the top exponent. -/

    {R : Cocycle Ω X} {L : ℕ∞} {lam : ℕ → EReal}
    {m : ℕ → ℕ+} {E : ∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → (i : ℕ∞) < L → Ω → GrassmannianFin X (m i)}
    {V : ℕ → Ω → Submodule ℝ X} {P : ℕ → Ω → X →L[ℝ] X}
    (h : IsOseledetsDecomposition R L lam m E V P) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), ∀ b : ℝ, lam 1 < (b : EReal) → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ‖R.iterate n ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω)‖ ≤ Real.exp (b * n)

/-- Backward upper growth on the slow spaces. -/
axiom backward_norm_slowSpace_le [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X]
    {R : Cocycle Ω X} {L : ℕ∞} {lam : ℕ → EReal}
    {m : ℕ → ℕ+} {E : ∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → (i : ℕ∞) < L → Ω → GrassmannianFin X (m i)}
    {V : ℕ → Ω → Submodule ℝ X} {P : ℕ → Ω → X →L[ℝ] X}
    (h : IsOseledetsDecomposition R L lam m E V P)
    {l : ℕ} (hl₁ : 2 ≤ l) (hl₂ : (l : ℕ∞) ≤ L) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), ∀ b : ℝ, lam l < (b : EReal) → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,

concepts.title: Backward histories
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a Banach space $X$ over $(\Omega, \sigma, \mu)$. A *backward
history* of $x \in X$ at $\omega$ is a sequence $y_0 = x, y_1, y_2, \ldots$ in $X$ with
$$\mathcal{L}_{\sigma^{-(n+1)}\omega}\, y_{n+1} = y_n \quad \text{for all } n \ge 0,$$
so that $\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\sigma^{-n}\omega}\, y_n = x$. For $c \in [-\infty, \infty]$,
$B_c(\omega)$ is the set of $x \in X$ having a backward history that decays at rate $c$:
$$\limsup_n \tfrac1n \log \|y_n\| \le -c,$$
that is, for every real $b < c$, $\|y_n\| \le e^{-bn}$ for all large $n$. In Lean
$\sigma^{-n}\omega$ is written `σ.symm^[n] ω`.

/-!
---
title: Backward histories
type: definition
---
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a Banach space $X$ over $(\Omega, \sigma, \mu)$. A *backward
history* of $x \in X$ at $\omega$ is a sequence $y_0 = x, y_1, y_2, \ldots$ in $X$ with
$$\mathcal{L}_{\sigma^{-(n+1)}\omega}\, y_{n+1} = y_n \quad \text{for all } n \ge 0,$$
so that $\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\sigma^{-n}\omega}\, y_n = x$. For $c \in [-\infty, \infty]$,
$B_c(\omega)$ is the set of $x \in X$ having a backward history that decays at rate $c$:
$$\limsup_n \tfrac1n \log \|y_n\| \le -c,$$
that is, for every real $b < c$, $\|y_n\| \le e^{-bn}$ for all large $n$. In Lean
$\sigma^{-n}\omega$ is written `σ.symm^[n] ω`.
-/

namespace Lax606786.BackwardHistories

open Filter
open Lax606786.Cocycles

/-- `B_c(ω)`: the vectors with a backward history along `σ^{-n}ω` decaying at rate `c`. -/
def backwardSet {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
    [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X]
    (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) (c : EReal) : Set X :=
  {x | ∃ y : ℕ → X, y 0 = x ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, R.L ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n + 1] ω) (y (n + 1)) = y n) ∧
    ∀ b : ℝ, (b : EReal) < c → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ‖y n‖ ≤ Real.exp (-b * n)}

end Lax606786.BackwardHistories

concepts.title: Vectors with decaying backward histories form subspaces
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a Banach space $X$, and $B_c(\omega)$ the set of vectors with a
backward history at $\omega$ decaying at rate $c$. Then

- each $B_c(\omega)$ is a linear subspace of $X$, and $B_c(\omega) \subseteq B_{c'}(\omega)$ for
  $c' \le c$;
- if $X$ is separable with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra and $E : \Omega \to \mathcal{G}_m X$ is a
  measurable family with $\mathcal{L}_\omega E(\omega) = E(\sigma\omega)$ almost surely, growing at
  rate at least $c$ (for every $b < c$, $g(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega, E(\omega)) \ge e^{bn}$ for all
  large $n$, almost surely), then $E(\omega) \subseteq B_c(\omega)$ almost surely.

concepts.title: The backward Vitali lemma
concepts.description:
Let $\sigma$ be an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a nonatomic standard
probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$. For $\omega \in \Omega$ and $j \in \mathbb{N}$ write $I_j(\omega)
= \{\sigma^i \omega : -j \le i \le j\}$ for the orbit window of radius $j$.

Let $\varepsilon > 0$, and let $j_1, j_2, \ldots : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$ be measurable with
$j_k(\omega) \to \infty$ for every $\omega$. Then there are a measurable set $A$ and a measurable
$j : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$ such that

- for every $\omega \in A$, $j(\omega) = j_k(\omega)$ for some $k$;
- the windows $I_{j(\omega)}(\omega)$, $\omega \in A$, are pairwise disjoint;
- $\mu\bigl(\bigcup_{\omega \in A} I_{j(\omega)}(\omega)\bigr) > 1 - \varepsilon$.

This is a form of Rudolph's backward Vitali lemma (Rudolph 1990, Theorem 3.9).

import Mathlib.Dynamics.Ergodic.Ergodic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Typeclasses.NullSingletonClass
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.Polish.Basic

/-!
---
title: The backward Vitali lemma
type: theorem
---
Let $\sigma$ be an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a nonatomic standard
probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$. For $\omega \in \Omega$ and $j \in \mathbb{N}$ write $I_j(\omega)
= \{\sigma^i \omega : -j \le i \le j\}$ for the orbit window of radius $j$.

Let $\varepsilon > 0$, and let $j_1, j_2, \ldots : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$ be measurable with
$j_k(\omega) \to \infty$ for every $\omega$. Then there are a measurable set $A$ and a measurable
$j : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$ such that

- for every $\omega \in A$, $j(\omega) = j_k(\omega)$ for some $k$;
- the windows $I_{j(\omega)}(\omega)$, $\omega \in A$, are pairwise disjoint;
- $\mu\bigl(\bigcup_{\omega \in A} I_{j(\omega)}(\omega)\bigr) > 1 - \varepsilon$.

This is a form of Rudolph's backward Vitali lemma (Rudolph 1990, Theorem 3.9).
-/

namespace Lax606786.BackwardVitali

open MeasureTheory Filter

/-- The orbit window `{σⁱ ω : -j ≤ i ≤ j}`. -/
def orbitWindow {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (σ : Ω ≃ᵐ Ω) (ω : Ω) (j : ℕ) : Set Ω :=
  {x | ∃ i ≤ j, x = σ^[i] ω ∨ x = (σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[i] ω}

/-- Disjoint orbit windows, of admissible radii, covering all but `ε` of the space. -/
axiom backwardVitali {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω)
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [NullSingletonClass μ] (σ : Ω ≃ᵐ Ω) (hσ : Ergodic σ μ)
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (j : ℕ → Ω → ℕ) (hj : ∀ k, Measurable (j k))
    (hjtop : ∀ ω, Tendsto (fun k => j k ω) atTop atTop) :
    ∃ (A : Set Ω) (jω : Ω → ℕ), MeasurableSet A ∧ Measurable jω ∧
      (∀ ω ∈ A, ∃ k, jω ω = j k ω) ∧
      (A.PairwiseDisjoint fun ω => orbitWindow σ ω (jω ω)) ∧
      ENNReal.ofReal (1 - ε) < μ (⋃ ω ∈ A, orbitWindow σ ω (jω ω))

end Lax606786.BackwardVitali

  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [MeasureTheory.NullSingletonClass μ] (σ : MeasurableEquiv Ω Ω),
  Ergodic (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe σ) μ →
    ∀ (ε : Real),
      Real.instLT.lt 0 ε →
        ∀ (j : Nat → Ω → Nat),
          (∀ (k : Nat), Measurable (j k)) →
            (∀ (ω : Ω), Filter.Tendsto (fun k => j k ω) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop) →

concepts.title: Kingman's theorem for balanced intervals
concepts.description:
Let $\sigma$ be an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a nonatomic standard
probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, and let $(f_n)$ be a subadditive family over $\sigma$ with
$f_1^+$ integrable. Then the averages over the balanced time intervals $[-n, n)$ converge to the
same constant as in Kingman's theorem:
$$\tfrac{1}{2n} f_{2n}(\sigma^{-n}\omega) \to C = \lim_{n \to \infty} \underline{\int}
  \tfrac1n f_n \, d\mu \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega,$$
with $C \in [-\infty, \infty)$, limits taken in the extended reals, and $\underline{\int}$ the
lower integral. This is Theorem 24 of Lee (2024).

Given that the forward averages $\frac1n f_n$ converge almost everywhere to a constant
$C \in [-\infty, \infty]$, the shifted averages $\frac1n f_n(\sigma^n\omega)$ and the balanced
averages converge to the same $C$.

import Lax606786.SubadditiveFamilies
import Lax606786.LowerIntegrals
import Mathlib.Dynamics.Ergodic.Ergodic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Typeclasses.NullSingletonClass
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.Polish.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.EReal.Operations

/-!
---
title: Kingman's theorem for balanced intervals
type: theorem
---
Let $\sigma$ be an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a nonatomic standard
probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, and let $(f_n)$ be a subadditive family over $\sigma$ with
$f_1^+$ integrable. Then the averages over the balanced time intervals $[-n, n)$ converge to the
same constant as in Kingman's theorem:
$$\tfrac{1}{2n} f_{2n}(\sigma^{-n}\omega) \to C = \lim_{n \to \infty} \underline{\int}
  \tfrac1n f_n \, d\mu \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega,$$
with $C \in [-\infty, \infty)$, limits taken in the extended reals, and $\underline{\int}$ the
lower integral. This is Theorem 24 of Lee (2024).

Given that the forward averages $\frac1n f_n$ converge almost everywhere to a constant
$C \in [-\infty, \infty]$, the shifted averages $\frac1n f_n(\sigma^n\omega)$ and the balanced
averages converge to the same $C$.
-/

namespace Lax606786.BalancedKingman

open MeasureTheory Filter Topology
open Lax606786.SubadditiveFamilies

/-- `f_{2n}(σ^{-n} ω) / 2n` converges almost everywhere to `C = lim (1/n) ∫ f_n`. -/
axiom balancedKingman {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [NullSingletonClass μ]
    (σ : Ω ≃ᵐ Ω) (hσ : Ergodic σ μ) (f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (hf : IsSubadditiveFamily σ f)
    (h1 : Integrable (fun ω => max (f 1 ω) 0) μ) :
    ∃ C : EReal, C < ⊤ ∧
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f (2 * n) ((σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω) / (2 * n) : EReal))
        atTop (𝓝 C)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Lax606786.LowerIntegrals.lowerIntegral μ (fun ω => f n ω / n)) atTop
        (𝓝 C)

/-- The forward, shifted and balanced averages all converge to the same constant. -/
axiom three_limits {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [NullSingletonClass μ] {σ : Ω ≃ᵐ Ω} (hσ : Ergodic (⇑σ) μ)
    {f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (hf : IsSubadditiveFamily (⇑σ) f)
    (h1 : Integrable (fun ω => max (f 1 ω) 0) μ) (C : EReal)
    (hC : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f n ω / n : EReal)) atTop (𝓝 C)) :
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f n (σ^[n] ω) / n : EReal)) atTop (𝓝 C)) ∧
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
        (f (2 * n) ((σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω) / (2 * n) : EReal)) atTop (𝓝 C))

end Lax606786.BalancedKingman

  Ergodic (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe σ) μ →

concepts.title: The Grassmannians of a Banach space
concepts.description:
Let $X$ be a real normed space. The unit sphere of a subspace $V \le X$ is
$\mathbb{S}_V = \{x \in V : \|x\| = 1\}$; it spans $V$, so it determines $V$.

- The Grassmannian $\mathcal{G} X$ is the set of closed subspaces $V \le X$ admitting a bounded
  projection $X \to V$. It carries the distance
  $$d(V, W) = d_H(\mathbb{S}_V, \mathbb{S}_W) \in [0, \infty],$$
  the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres (infinite exactly when one of $V, W$ is $0$ and
  the other is not).
- For $k \ge 0$, $\mathcal{G}^k X$ is the set of $V \in \mathcal{G} X$ of codimension $k$, that
  is, with $\dim(X/V) = k$.
- For $k \ge 0$, $\mathcal{G}_k X$ is the set of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $X$. For
  $k \ge 1$ the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}_V$ is a nonempty compact set and $\mathcal{G}_k X$
  carries the metric $d(V, W) = d_H(\mathbb{S}_V, \mathbb{S}_W)$.

Each is equipped with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of its distance.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Analysis.RCLike.Lemmas
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.Closeds
import Mathlib.Analysis.LocallyConvex.HahnBanach
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.HahnBanach

/-!
---
title: The Grassmannians of a Banach space
type: definition
---
Let $X$ be a real normed space. The unit sphere of a subspace $V \le X$ is
$\mathbb{S}_V = \{x \in V : \|x\| = 1\}$; it spans $V$, so it determines $V$.

- The Grassmannian $\mathcal{G} X$ is the set of closed subspaces $V \le X$ admitting a bounded
  projection $X \to V$. It carries the distance
  $$d(V, W) = d_H(\mathbb{S}_V, \mathbb{S}_W) \in [0, \infty],$$
  the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres (infinite exactly when one of $V, W$ is $0$ and
  the other is not).
- For $k \ge 0$, $\mathcal{G}^k X$ is the set of $V \in \mathcal{G} X$ of codimension $k$, that
  is, with $\dim(X/V) = k$.
- For $k \ge 0$, $\mathcal{G}_k X$ is the set of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $X$. For
  $k \ge 1$ the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}_V$ is a nonempty compact set and $\mathcal{G}_k X$
  carries the metric $d(V, W) = d_H(\mathbb{S}_V, \mathbb{S}_W)$.

Each is equipped with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of its distance.
-/

namespace Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian

open TopologicalSpace

variable (X : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]

/-- `𝒢X`: the closed subspaces of `X` admitting a bounded projection onto them. -/
def Grassmannian : Type _ :=
  {V : Submodule ℝ X // V.ClosedComplemented}

variable {X}

/-- Every subspace is spanned by its unit sphere. -/
theorem span_sphere_inter (V : Submodule ℝ X) :
    Submodule.span ℝ (Metric.sphere (0 : X) 1 ∩ (V : Set X)) = V := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact Submodule.span_le.2 Set.inter_subset_right
  · intro x hx
    rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
    · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
    · have hxeq : x = ‖x‖ • (‖x‖⁻¹ • x) := by
        rw [smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0), one_smul]
      rw [hxeq]
      refine Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨?_, V.smul_mem _ hx⟩)
      rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
        inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0)]

namespace Grassmannian

/-- The unit sphere `𝕊_V = {x ∈ V : ‖x‖ = 1}`. -/
def sphere (V : Grassmannian X) : Set X :=
  Metric.sphere (0 : X) 1 ∩ (V.1 : Set X)

/-- `V ↦ 𝕊_V`, as a closed subset of `X`. -/
def toCloseds (V : Grassmannian X) : Closeds X :=
  ⟨V.sphere, Metric.isClosed_sphere.inter V.2.isClosed⟩

/-- A subspace is the span of its unit sphere, so `V ↦ 𝕊_V` is injective. -/
theorem toCloseds_injective : Function.Injective (toCloseds (X := X)) := by
  intro V W h
  apply Subtype.ext
  rw [← span_sphere_inter V.1, ← span_sphere_inter W.1]
  exact congrArg (fun s : Closeds X => Submodule.span ℝ (s : Set X)) h

/-- The distance on `𝒢X`: the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres. -/
noncomputable instance instEMetricSpace : EMetricSpace (Grassmannian X) :=
  EMetricSpace.induced toCloseds toCloseds_injective inferInstance

/-- The Borel `σ`-algebra of that distance. -/
noncomputable instance instMeasurableSpace : MeasurableSpace (Grassmannian X) :=
  borel (Grassmannian X)

instance instBorelSpace : BorelSpace (Grassmannian X) := ⟨rfl⟩

/-- `𝕊_V` is closed. -/
theorem isClosed_sphere (V : Grassmannian X) : IsClosed V.sphere :=
  Metric.isClosed_sphere.inter V.2.isClosed

end Grassmannian

variable (X)

/-- `𝒢^k X`: the subspaces in `𝒢X` of codimension `k`. -/
def GrassmannianCofin (k : ℕ) : Type _ :=
  {V : Grassmannian X // FiniteDimensional ℝ (X ⧸ (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) ∧
    Module.finrank ℝ (X ⧸ (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) = k}

/-- `𝒢_k X`: the `k`-dimensional subspaces of `X`. -/
def GrassmannianFin (k : ℕ) : Type _ :=
  {V : Submodule ℝ X // FiniteDimensional ℝ V ∧ Module.finrank ℝ V = k}

variable {X}

namespace GrassmannianFin

/-- The unit sphere `𝕊_V = {x ∈ V : ‖x‖ = 1}`. -/
def sphere {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : Set X :=
  Metric.sphere (0 : X) 1 ∩ (V.1 : Set X)

/-- `V` is the span of its unit sphere. -/
theorem span_sphere {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) :
    Submodule.span ℝ V.sphere = (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact Submodule.span_le.2 Set.inter_subset_right
  · intro x hx
    rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
    · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
    · have hxeq : x = ‖x‖ • (‖x‖⁻¹ • x) := by
        rw [smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0), one_smul]
      rw [hxeq]
      refine Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨?_, V.1.smul_mem _ hx⟩)
      rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
        inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0)]

/-- `𝕊_V` is compact. -/
theorem isCompact_sphere {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : IsCompact V.sphere := by
  have : FiniteDimensional ℝ (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) := V.2.1
  have himg : V.sphere =
      (Subtype.val : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) → X) '' Metric.sphere (0 : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) 1 := by
    ext x
    simp only [sphere, Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_image]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hx1, hxV⟩
      refine ⟨⟨x, hxV⟩, ?_, rfl⟩
      rwa [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm] at hx1 ⊢
    · rintro ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩
      rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm] at hv
      exact ⟨by rwa [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm], v.2⟩
  rw [himg]
  exact (_root_.isCompact_sphere (0 : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) 1).image continuous_subtype_val

/-- `𝕊_V` is nonempty when `k ≠ 0`. -/
theorem nonempty_sphere {k : ℕ} [NeZero k] (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : V.sphere.Nonempty := by
  have hne : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) ≠ ⊥ := by
    intro h
    apply NeZero.ne k
    have hfr := V.2.2
    rw [h, finrank_bot] at hfr
    exact hfr.symm
  obtain ⟨x, hxV, hx0⟩ := Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot hne
  refine ⟨‖x‖⁻¹ • x, ?_, V.1.smul_mem _ hxV⟩
  rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
    inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0)]

/-- `V ↦ 𝕊_V`, as a nonempty compact subset of `X`. -/
noncomputable def toNonemptyCompacts {k : ℕ} [NeZero k] (V : GrassmannianFin X k) :
    NonemptyCompacts X where
  carrier := V.sphere
  isCompact' := V.isCompact_sphere
  nonempty' := V.nonempty_sphere

/-- A subspace is the span of its unit sphere, so `V ↦ 𝕊_V` is injective. -/
theorem toNonemptyCompacts_injective (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] :
    Function.Injective (toNonemptyCompacts (X := X) (k := k)) := by
  intro V W h
  apply Subtype.ext
  rw [← V.span_sphere, ← W.span_sphere]
  exact congrArg (fun s : NonemptyCompacts X => Submodule.span ℝ (s : Set X)) h

/-- The metric on `𝒢_k X`: the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres. -/
noncomputable instance instMetricSpace (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] : MetricSpace (GrassmannianFin X k) :=
  MetricSpace.induced toNonemptyCompacts (toNonemptyCompacts_injective k) inferInstance

/-- The Borel `σ`-algebra of that metric. -/
noncomputable instance instMeasurableSpace (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] :
    MeasurableSpace (GrassmannianFin X k) :=
  borel (GrassmannianFin X k)

instance instBorelSpace (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] : BorelSpace (GrassmannianFin X k) := ⟨rfl⟩

/-- `V` is recovered from `𝕊_V`. -/
theorem sphere_injective (k : ℕ) : Function.Injective (sphere (X := X) (k := k)) := by
  intro V W h
  apply Subtype.ext
  rw [← V.span_sphere, ← W.span_sphere, h]

/-- A finite-dimensional subspace admits a bounded projection onto it, so `𝒢_k X` sits inside
`𝒢 X`. -/
theorem closedComplemented {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) :
    (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X).ClosedComplemented := by
  have : FiniteDimensional ℝ (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) := V.2.1
  exact Submodule.ClosedComplemented.of_finiteDimensional _

/-- The inclusion `𝒢_k X → 𝒢 X`. -/
def toGrassmannian {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : Grassmannian X :=
  ⟨V.1, V.closedComplemented⟩

end GrassmannianFin

end Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian

concepts.title: Elementary properties of Bernstein numbers
concepts.description:
Let $X$ be a real normed space and $S, T$ bounded operators on $X$.

- $\rho_0(T) = 0$, $\rho_1(T) = \|T\|$, $0 \le \rho_k(T) \le \|T\|$, and
  $\rho_q(T) \le \rho_p(T)$ for $1 \le p \le q$.
- $g(T, V) \le \rho_m(T)$ for every $V \in \mathcal{G}_m X$, and
  $\rho_1(T) \cdots \rho_k(T) \le \|T\|^k$.

For every $k$,
$$\rho_k(S T) \le \rho_k(S)\,\|T\| \qquad \text{and} \qquad \rho_k(S T) \le \|S\|\,\rho_k(T).$$
Moreover, for $k \ge 1$ the growth $g(T, V)$ is jointly continuous in $(T, V)$, for the operator
norm on $T$ and the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres on $V \in \mathcal{G}_k X$.

import Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

/-!
---
title: Elementary properties of Bernstein numbers
type: theorem
---
Let $X$ be a real normed space and $S, T$ bounded operators on $X$.

- $\rho_0(T) = 0$, $\rho_1(T) = \|T\|$, $0 \le \rho_k(T) \le \|T\|$, and
  $\rho_q(T) \le \rho_p(T)$ for $1 \le p \le q$.
- $g(T, V) \le \rho_m(T)$ for every $V \in \mathcal{G}_m X$, and
  $\rho_1(T) \cdots \rho_k(T) \le \|T\|^k$.

For every $k$,
$$\rho_k(S T) \le \rho_k(S)\,\|T\| \qquad \text{and} \qquad \rho_k(S T) \le \|S\|\,\rho_k(T).$$
Moreover, for $k \ge 1$ the growth $g(T, V)$ is jointly continuous in $(T, V)$, for the operator
norm on $T$ and the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres on $V \in \mathcal{G}_k X$.
-/

namespace Lax606786.BernsteinNumberProperties

open Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

variable {X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]

/-- `ρ_k(T) ≥ 0`. -/
axiom bernsteinNumber_nonneg (T : X →L[ℝ] X) (k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ bernsteinNumber T k

/-- `ρ_0(T) = 0`. -/
axiom bernsteinNumber_zero (T : X →L[ℝ] X) : bernsteinNumber T 0 = 0

/-- `ρ_1(T) = ‖T‖`. -/
axiom bernsteinNumber_one (T : X →L[ℝ] X) : bernsteinNumber T 1 = ‖T‖

/-- `ρ_k(T) ≤ ‖T‖`. -/
axiom bernsteinNumber_le_opNorm (T : X →L[ℝ] X) (k : ℕ) : bernsteinNumber T k ≤ ‖T‖

/-- `ρ_q(T) ≤ ρ_p(T)` for `1 ≤ p ≤ q`. -/
axiom bernsteinNumber_antitone (T : X →L[ℝ] X) {p q : ℕ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hpq : p ≤ q) :
    bernsteinNumber T q ≤ bernsteinNumber T p

/-- `g(T, V) ≤ ρ_m(T)` for `V ∈ 𝒢_m X`. -/
axiom growth_le_bernsteinNumber {m : ℕ} (T : X →L[ℝ] X) (V : GrassmannianFin X m) :
    growth T (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) ≤ bernsteinNumber T m

/-- `ρ_1(T) ⋯ ρ_k(T) ≤ ‖T‖^k`. -/

concepts.title: Birkhoff's pointwise ergodic theorem
concepts.description:
Let $\sigma$ be a measure-preserving transformation of a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ and let
$f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable. Let $\mathcal{I}$ be the $\sigma$-algebra of measurable
sets $A$ with $\sigma^{-1} A = A$. Then the Birkhoff averages converge almost everywhere and in
$L^1(\mu)$ to the conditional expectation of $f$ given $\mathcal{I}$:
$$\frac1n \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(\sigma^k \omega) \to \mathbb{E}[f \mid \mathcal{I}](\omega)
  \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega, \qquad
  \Bigl\| \frac1n \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f \circ \sigma^k - \mathbb{E}[f \mid \mathcal{I}] \Bigr\|_1
  \to 0.$$
When $\sigma$ is ergodic, $\mathcal{I}$ is trivial and the limit is the constant $\int f \, d\mu$.

The almost-everywhere convergence is due to Birkhoff (1931). Convergence in mean goes back to von
Neumann (1932), who proved it in $L^2$.

import Mathlib.Dynamics.BirkhoffSum.Average
import Mathlib.Dynamics.Ergodic.Ergodic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.Invariants

/-!
---
title: Birkhoff's pointwise ergodic theorem
type: theorem
---
Let $\sigma$ be a measure-preserving transformation of a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ and let
$f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable. Let $\mathcal{I}$ be the $\sigma$-algebra of measurable
sets $A$ with $\sigma^{-1} A = A$. Then the Birkhoff averages converge almost everywhere and in
$L^1(\mu)$ to the conditional expectation of $f$ given $\mathcal{I}$:
$$\frac1n \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(\sigma^k \omega) \to \mathbb{E}[f \mid \mathcal{I}](\omega)
  \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega, \qquad
  \Bigl\| \frac1n \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f \circ \sigma^k - \mathbb{E}[f \mid \mathcal{I}] \Bigr\|_1
  \to 0.$$
When $\sigma$ is ergodic, $\mathcal{I}$ is trivial and the limit is the constant $\int f \, d\mu$.

The almost-everywhere convergence is due to Birkhoff (1931). Convergence in mean goes back to von
Neumann (1932), who proved it in $L^2$.
-/

namespace Lax606786.BirkhoffErgodicTheorem

open MeasureTheory Filter Topology

/-- The Birkhoff averages converge a.e. and in `L¹` to the conditional expectation of `f` given
the `σ`-algebra of `σ`-invariant sets. -/
axiom birkhoff {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (σ : Ω → Ω) (hσ : MeasurePreserving σ μ μ) (f : Ω → ℝ) (hf : Integrable f μ) :
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => birkhoffAverage ℝ σ f n ω) atTop
      (𝓝 ((μ[f | MeasurableSpace.invariants σ]) ω))) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
      ∫ ω, |birkhoffAverage ℝ σ f n ω - (μ[f | MeasurableSpace.invariants σ]) ω| ∂μ)
      atTop (𝓝 0)

/-- For an ergodic transformation the Birkhoff averages of an integrable function converge almost
everywhere to its integral. -/
axiom birkhoff_of_ergodic {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω)
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (σ : Ω → Ω) (hσ : Ergodic σ μ) (f : Ω → ℝ) (hf : Integrable f μ) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => birkhoffAverage ℝ σ f n ω) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂μ))

end Lax606786.BirkhoffErgodicTheorem

  (σ : Ω → Ω),
  MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving σ μ μ →
    ∀ (f : Ω → Real),
      MeasureTheory.Integrable f μ →
        And
          (Filter.Eventually
            (fun ω =>
              Filter.Tendsto (fun n => birkhoffAverage Real σ f n ω) Filter.atTop
                (nhds (MeasureTheory.condExp (MeasurableSpace.invariants σ) μ f ω)))
            (MeasureTheory.ae μ))
          (Filter.Tendsto
            (fun n =>
              MeasureTheory.integral μ fun ω =>
                abs
                  (instHSub.hSub (birkhoffAverage Real σ f n ω)
                    (MeasureTheory.condExp (MeasurableSpace.invariants σ) μ f ω)))
            Filter.atTop (nhds 0))

concepts.title: Measurability of iterates, and constancy of the Lyapunov exponents
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$ with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra.

- Each iterate is strongly measurable: $\omega \mapsto \mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega x$ is measurable
  for every $n$ and $x$.
- For every $k$ the exponent $\chi_k$ is almost everywhere equal to a constant; so are the
  distinct exponents $\lambda_i$ and their multiplicities $m_i$.

import Lax606786.Cocycles

/-!
---
title: Measurability of iterates, and constancy of the Lyapunov exponents
type: theorem
---
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$ with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra.

- Each iterate is strongly measurable: $\omega \mapsto \mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega x$ is measurable
  for every $n$ and $x$.
- For every $k$ the exponent $\chi_k$ is almost everywhere equal to a constant; so are the
  distinct exponents $\lambda_i$ and their multiplicities $m_i$.
-/

namespace Lax606786.CocycleBasics

open MeasureTheory TopologicalSpace
open Lax606786.Cocycles

variable {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
  [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X]

/-- The iterates are strongly measurable. -/
axiom measurable_iterate_apply (R : Cocycle Ω X) [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
    (n : ℕ) (x : X) : Measurable fun ω => R.iterate n ω x

/-- `χ_k` is a.e. constant. -/
axiom exists_chi_ae_eq (R : Cocycle Ω X) [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ c : EReal, ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.chi k ω = c

/-- The distinct exponent `λ_i` is a.e. constant. -/
axiom exists_lambda_ae_eq (R : Cocycle Ω X) [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (i : ℕ) :
    ∃ c : EReal, ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.lambda i ω = c

/-- The multiplicity `m_i` is a.e. constant. -/
axiom exists_mult_ae_eq (R : Cocycle Ω X) [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (i : ℕ) :
    ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.mult i ω = m

end Lax606786.CocycleBasics

concepts.title: Elementary identities for iterates of a cocycle
concepts.description:
The following elementary identities hold for a cocycle $\mathcal{L}$ over $(\Omega, \sigma, \mu)$,
along forward and backward orbits; they are used throughout.

- $\mathcal{L}^{(1)}_\omega = \mathcal{L}_\omega$ and
  $\mathcal{L}^{(m+n)}_\omega = \mathcal{L}^{(m)}_{\sigma^n\omega} \mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega$ (the
  cocycle law), in particular
  $\mathcal{L}^{(n+1)}_\omega = \mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\sigma\omega}\mathcal{L}_\omega$;
- $\sigma^j \sigma^{-(j+n)}\omega = \sigma^{-n}\omega$;
- if $E$ is a family of $m$-dimensional subspaces with
  $\mathcal{L}_{\sigma^k\omega}E(\sigma^k\omega) = E(\sigma^{k+1}\omega)$ for every $k$, then
  $\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega E(\omega) = E(\sigma^n\omega)$ for every $n$;
- if $(y_n)$ is a backward history at $\omega$, that is
  $\mathcal{L}_{\sigma^{-(n+1)}\omega}\, y_{n+1} = y_n$ for all $n$, then
  $\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\sigma^{-n}\omega}\, y_n = y_0$;
- if subspaces $W(\zeta)$ satisfy $\mathcal{L}_{\sigma^{-(m+1)}\omega} W(\sigma^{-(m+1)}\omega)
  \subseteq W(\sigma^{-m}\omega)$ for all $m$, then
  $\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\sigma^{-n}\omega} W(\sigma^{-n}\omega) \subseteq W(\omega)$;
- an almost-everywhere property holds almost everywhere at every point of the backward orbit.

import Lax606786.Cocycles
import Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian

/-!
---
title: Elementary identities for iterates of a cocycle
type: theorem
---
The following elementary identities hold for a cocycle $\mathcal{L}$ over $(\Omega, \sigma, \mu)$,
along forward and backward orbits; they are used throughout.

- $\mathcal{L}^{(1)}_\omega = \mathcal{L}_\omega$ and
  $\mathcal{L}^{(m+n)}_\omega = \mathcal{L}^{(m)}_{\sigma^n\omega} \mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega$ (the
  cocycle law), in particular
  $\mathcal{L}^{(n+1)}_\omega = \mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\sigma\omega}\mathcal{L}_\omega$;
- $\sigma^j \sigma^{-(j+n)}\omega = \sigma^{-n}\omega$;
- if $E$ is a family of $m$-dimensional subspaces with
  $\mathcal{L}_{\sigma^k\omega}E(\sigma^k\omega) = E(\sigma^{k+1}\omega)$ for every $k$, then
  $\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega E(\omega) = E(\sigma^n\omega)$ for every $n$;
- if $(y_n)$ is a backward history at $\omega$, that is
  $\mathcal{L}_{\sigma^{-(n+1)}\omega}\, y_{n+1} = y_n$ for all $n$, then
  $\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\sigma^{-n}\omega}\, y_n = y_0$;
- if subspaces $W(\zeta)$ satisfy $\mathcal{L}_{\sigma^{-(m+1)}\omega} W(\sigma^{-(m+1)}\omega)
  \subseteq W(\sigma^{-m}\omega)$ for all $m$, then
  $\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\sigma^{-n}\omega} W(\sigma^{-n}\omega) \subseteq W(\omega)$;
- an almost-everywhere property holds almost everywhere at every point of the backward orbit.
-/

namespace Lax606786.CocycleIterates

open MeasureTheory
open Lax606786.Cocycles Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian

variable {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
  [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X]

/-- `𝓛^{(1)}_ω = 𝓛_ω`. -/
axiom iterate_one (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) : R.iterate 1 ω = R.L ω

/-- The cocycle law `𝓛^{(m+n)}_ω = 𝓛^{(m)}_{σⁿω} ∘ 𝓛^{(n)}_ω`. -/
axiom iterate_add (R : Cocycle Ω X) (m n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    R.iterate (m + n) ω = (R.iterate m (R.σ^[n] ω)).comp (R.iterate n ω)

/-- `𝓛^{(n+1)}_ω = 𝓛^{(n)}_{σω} ∘ 𝓛_ω`. -/
axiom iterate_succ_left (R : Cocycle Ω X) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    R.iterate (n + 1) ω = (R.iterate n (R.σ ω)).comp (R.L ω)

/-- `σ^j σ^{-(j+n)} ω = σ^{-n} ω`. -/
axiom iterate_sigma_symm_iterate (R : Cocycle Ω X) (j n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    (R.σ : Ω → Ω)^[j] ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[j + n] ω) = (R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω

/-- An equivariant family is carried along by the iterates. -/
axiom map_iterate_of_equivariant (R : Cocycle Ω X) {m : ℕ} [NeZero m]
    (E : Ω → GrassmannianFin X m) (ω : Ω)
    (h : ∀ k : ℕ, Submodule.map (R.L (R.σ^[k] ω) : X →ₗ[ℝ] X)
        ((E (R.σ^[k] ω)).1 : Submodule ℝ X) = ((E (R.σ^[k + 1] ω)).1 : Submodule ℝ X))
    (n : ℕ) :
    Submodule.map (R.iterate n ω : X →ₗ[ℝ] X) ((E ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)
      = ((E (R.σ^[n] ω)).1 : Submodule ℝ X)

/-- A backward history is carried back to its start by the iterates. -/
axiom iterate_history (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) {y : ℕ → X}
    (hyL : ∀ n : ℕ, R.L ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n + 1] ω) (y (n + 1)) = y n) (n : ℕ) :
    R.iterate n ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω) (y n) = y 0

/-- A family invariant along the backward orbit is carried forward by the iterates. -/
axiom iterate_mem_of_backward (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) (W : Ω → Submodule ℝ X)
    (hW : ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ x ∈ W ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[m + 1] ω),
      R.L ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[m + 1] ω) x ∈ W ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[m] ω)) :
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ x ∈ W ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω),
      R.iterate n ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω) x ∈ W ω

/-- An a.e. property holds a.e. at every point of the backward orbit. -/
axiom ae_forall_iterate_symm (R : Cocycle Ω X) {p : Ω → Prop} (hp : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), p ω) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), ∀ k : ℕ, p ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[k] ω)

end Lax606786.CocycleIterates

concepts.title: Cocycles and their Lyapunov exponents
concepts.description:
A **cocycle** consists of an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation $\sigma$ of a
nonatomic standard probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, together with a map $\omega \mapsto
\mathcal{L}_\omega$ from $\Omega$ into the bounded operators on a real Banach space $X$ which is

- *strongly measurable*: $\omega \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\omega x$ is measurable for each $x \in X$;
- *forward integrable*: $\log^+ \|\mathcal{L}_\omega\| \in L^1(\mu)$.

No invertibility of $\mathcal{L}_\omega$ is assumed. Its iterates are
$\mathcal{L}^{(0)}_\omega = \mathrm{id}$ and
$\mathcal{L}^{(n+1)}_\omega = \mathcal{L}_{\sigma^n \omega} \circ \mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega$.

All logarithms below take values in $[-\infty, \infty)$ with $\log 0 = -\infty$. Exponents and
multiplicities are indexed from $1$, as usual; the value at index $0$ is not used.

- The **growth rate of a vector** is
  $\lambda_\omega(x) = \limsup_n \frac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega x\|$.
- The **$k$-th Lyapunov exponent** ($k \ge 1$) is
  $\chi_k(\omega) = \limsup_n \frac1n \log \rho_k(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega)$, with
  $\rho_k$ the Bernstein number. The sequence $\chi_1 \ge \chi_2 \ge \cdots$ is non-increasing and
  $\chi_1 = \lambda_1$ is the top exponent.
- The **distinct exponents** $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdots$ are the distinct values of
  $\chi_k$: $\lambda_1 = \chi_1$ and $\lambda_{i+1} = \chi_t$ for the least $t$ with
  $\chi_t < \lambda_i$. The **multiplicity** $m_i$ of $\lambda_i$ is the number of $k$ with
  $\chi_k = \lambda_i$. When there is no exponent after $\lambda_i$ the recursion stops: $m_i$ is
  recorded as $0$, and the later $\lambda$'s are $-\infty$ (the index at which they would start
  is recorded as $0$, and $\chi_0 = -\infty$).
- The **Bernstein index** is $\nu(\omega) = \lim_k \chi_k(\omega) = \inf_k \chi_k(\omega)$. It stands in
  for the usual index of compactness, the growth rate of $\|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|_c$; the
  concept `IndexOfCompactness` shows that the two agree.
- The cocycle is **quasicompact** if $\nu < \lambda_1$ almost everywhere.
- A family of operators $\omega \mapsto P_\omega$ is **tempered** if
  $\omega \mapsto \log \|P_\omega\|$ is tempered for $(\sigma, \mu)$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax606786.ExtendedLog
import Lax606786.OperatorStatistics
import Lax606786.TemperedFunctions
import Mathlib.Dynamics.Ergodic.Ergodic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L1Space.Integrable

/-!
---
title: Cocycles and their Lyapunov exponents
type: definition
---
A **cocycle** consists of an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation $\sigma$ of a
nonatomic standard probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, together with a map $\omega \mapsto
\mathcal{L}_\omega$ from $\Omega$ into the bounded operators on a real Banach space $X$ which is

- *strongly measurable*: $\omega \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\omega x$ is measurable for each $x \in X$;
- *forward integrable*: $\log^+ \|\mathcal{L}_\omega\| \in L^1(\mu)$.

No invertibility of $\mathcal{L}_\omega$ is assumed. Its iterates are
$\mathcal{L}^{(0)}_\omega = \mathrm{id}$ and
$\mathcal{L}^{(n+1)}_\omega = \mathcal{L}_{\sigma^n \omega} \circ \mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega$.

All logarithms below take values in $[-\infty, \infty)$ with $\log 0 = -\infty$. Exponents and
multiplicities are indexed from $1$, as usual; the value at index $0$ is not used.

- The **growth rate of a vector** is
  $\lambda_\omega(x) = \limsup_n \frac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega x\|$.
- The **$k$-th Lyapunov exponent** ($k \ge 1$) is
  $\chi_k(\omega) = \limsup_n \frac1n \log \rho_k(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega)$, with
  $\rho_k$ the Bernstein number. The sequence $\chi_1 \ge \chi_2 \ge \cdots$ is non-increasing and
  $\chi_1 = \lambda_1$ is the top exponent.
- The **distinct exponents** $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdots$ are the distinct values of
  $\chi_k$: $\lambda_1 = \chi_1$ and $\lambda_{i+1} = \chi_t$ for the least $t$ with
  $\chi_t < \lambda_i$. The **multiplicity** $m_i$ of $\lambda_i$ is the number of $k$ with
  $\chi_k = \lambda_i$. When there is no exponent after $\lambda_i$ the recursion stops: $m_i$ is
  recorded as $0$, and the later $\lambda$'s are $-\infty$ (the index at which they would start
  is recorded as $0$, and $\chi_0 = -\infty$).
- The **Bernstein index** is $\nu(\omega) = \lim_k \chi_k(\omega) = \inf_k \chi_k(\omega)$. It stands in
  for the usual index of compactness, the growth rate of $\|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|_c$; the
  concept `IndexOfCompactness` shows that the two agree.
- The cocycle is **quasicompact** if $\nu < \lambda_1$ almost everywhere.
- A family of operators $\omega \mapsto P_\omega$ is **tempered** if
  $\omega \mapsto \log \|P_\omega\|$ is tempered for $(\sigma, \mu)$.
-/

namespace Lax606786.Cocycles

open MeasureTheory Filter
open Lax606786.OperatorStatistics Lax606786.ExtendedLog Lax606786.TemperedFunctions

variable {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
  [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X]

/-- A strongly measurable, forward-integrable cocycle of bounded operators on `X` over an
invertible ergodic transformation of a Lebesgue probability space. -/
structure Cocycle (Ω X : Type*) [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
    [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X] where
  /-- The base transformation, a measurable bijection with measurable inverse. -/
  σ : Ω ≃ᵐ Ω
  /-- The invariant measure. -/
  μ : Measure Ω
  /-- The generator `ω ↦ 𝓛_ω`. -/
  L : Ω → X →L[ℝ] X
  isProbability : IsProbabilityMeasure μ
  nullSingleton : NullSingletonClass μ
  ergodic : Ergodic σ μ
  stronglyMeasurable : ∀ x : X, Measurable (fun ω => L ω x)
  forwardIntegrable : Integrable (fun ω => Real.log (max ‖L ω‖ 1)) μ

attribute [instance] Cocycle.isProbability Cocycle.nullSingleton

namespace Cocycle

/-- `𝓛^{(n)}_ω = 𝓛_{σ^{n-1}ω} ∘ ⋯ ∘ 𝓛_ω`. -/
noncomputable def iterate (R : Cocycle Ω X) : ℕ → Ω → X →L[ℝ] X
  | 0, _ => ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ X
  | n + 1, ω => (R.L (R.σ^[n] ω)).comp (R.iterate n ω)

/-- `λ_ω(x) = limsup (1/n) log ‖𝓛^{(n)}_ω x‖`. -/
noncomputable def lambdaAt (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) (x : X) : EReal :=
  limsup (fun n : ℕ => logEReal ‖R.iterate n ω x‖ / (n : EReal)) atTop

/-- `χ_k(ω) = limsup (1/n) log ρ_k(𝓛^{(n)}_ω)`. Meaningful for `k ≥ 1`; `χ_0 = -∞`. -/
noncomputable def chi (R : Cocycle Ω X) (k : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : EReal :=
  limsup (fun n : ℕ => logEReal (bernsteinNumber (R.iterate n ω) k) / (n : EReal)) atTop

/-- The index `k` at which the distinct exponent `λ_i` first occurs among the `χ_k`: `1` for
`i = 1`, then the least `t ≥ 1` with `χ_t` below `λ_{i-1}`, and `0` once there is none. Index `0` is
not used. -/
noncomputable def lambdaIdx (R : Cocycle Ω X) : ℕ → Ω → ℕ
  | 0, _ => 0
  | 1, _ => 1
  | (i + 2), ω => sInf {t : ℕ | 1 ≤ t ∧ R.chi t ω < R.chi (R.lambdaIdx (i + 1) ω) ω}

/-- The distinct exponent `λ_i` (for `i ≥ 1`). -/
noncomputable def lambda (R : Cocycle Ω X) (i : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : EReal :=
  R.chi (R.lambdaIdx i ω) ω

/-- The multiplicity `m_i` of `λ_i` (for `i ≥ 1`); `0` if there is no exponent `λ_i`. -/
noncomputable def mult (R : Cocycle Ω X) (i : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : ℕ :=
  R.lambdaIdx (i + 1) ω - R.lambdaIdx i ω

/-- The Bernstein index `ν(ω) = inf_{k ≥ 1} χ_k(ω)`. -/
noncomputable def nu (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) : EReal := ⨅ k : ℕ, R.chi (k + 1) ω

/-- `ν < λ₁` almost everywhere. -/
def IsQuasicompact (R : Cocycle Ω X) : Prop :=
  ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.nu ω < R.chi 1 ω

/-- `ω ↦ log ‖P_ω‖` is tempered. -/
abbrev IsTempered (R : Cocycle Ω X) (P : Ω → X →L[ℝ] X) : Prop :=
  Tempered R.σ R.μ (fun ω => Real.log ‖P ω‖)

end Cocycle

end Lax606786.Cocycles

concepts.title: The exponents of an Oseledets decomposition
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a real normed space and $(L, \lambda, m, E, V, \Pi)$ an
Oseledets decomposition of it. Then the exponents strictly decrease,
$\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdots > \lambda_L$, the top exponent satisfies $\lambda_1 < \infty$, and
every exponent $\lambda_i$ with $i < L$ (one carrying a fast space) is a real number. Only the last
exponent $\lambda_L$ may be $-\infty$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax606786.OseledetsDecompositions

/-!
---
title: The exponents of an Oseledets decomposition
type: theorem
---
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a real normed space and $(L, \lambda, m, E, V, \Pi)$ an
Oseledets decomposition of it. Then the exponents strictly decrease,
$\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdots > \lambda_L$, the top exponent satisfies $\lambda_1 < \infty$, and
every exponent $\lambda_i$ with $i < L$ (one carrying a fast space) is a real number. Only the last
exponent $\lambda_L$ may be $-\infty$.

-/

namespace Lax606786.DecompositionExponents

open TopologicalSpace
open Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian Lax606786.Cocycles Lax606786.OseledetsDecompositions

variable {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
  [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X]
  {R : Cocycle Ω X} {L : ℕ∞} {lam : ℕ → EReal} {m : ℕ → ℕ+}
  {E : ∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → (i : ℕ∞) < L → Ω → GrassmannianFin X (m i)}
  {V : ℕ → Ω → Submodule ℝ X} {P : ℕ → Ω → X →L[ℝ] X}

/-- The exponents strictly decrease. -/
axiom lam_succ_lt (h : IsOseledetsDecomposition R L lam m E V P) {l : ℕ}
    (hl₁ : 1 ≤ l) (hl₂ : ((l + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ L) : lam (l + 1) < lam l

/-- Every exponent is at most the top one. -/
axiom lam_le_lam_one (h : IsOseledetsDecomposition R L lam m E V P) {l : ℕ}
    (hl₁ : 1 ≤ l) (hl₂ : (l : ℕ∞) ≤ L) : lam l ≤ lam 1

/-- The top exponent is less than `∞`. -/
axiom lam_one_lt_top (h : IsOseledetsDecomposition R L lam m E V P) : lam 1 < ⊤

/-- An exponent carrying a fast space is finite. -/
axiom lam_ne_bot_ne_top (h : IsOseledetsDecomposition R L lam m E V P) {l : ℕ}
    (hl₁ : 1 ≤ l) (hl₂ : (l : ℕ∞) < L) : lam l ≠ ⊥ ∧ lam l ≠ ⊤

end Lax606786.DecompositionExponents

concepts.title: The Lyapunov exponents are limits, forwards, backwards and over balanced intervals
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$ with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and
$k \ge 1$. Then $\chi_k$ is measurable, and for almost every $\omega$ the $\limsup$ defining it is a
limit, along forward orbits, along backward orbits and over balanced intervals:
$$\chi_k(\omega) = \lim_n \tfrac1n \log \rho_k(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega)
  = \lim_n \tfrac1n \log \rho_k(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\sigma^{-n}\omega})
  = \lim_n \tfrac1{2n} \log \rho_k(\mathcal{L}^{(2n)}_{\sigma^{-n}\omega}).$$
Moreover $\chi_1 \ge \chi_2 \ge \cdots$ pointwise, $\nu \le \chi_k$, and almost everywhere
$\chi_1 \le \int \log^+ \|\mathcal{L}\| \, d\mu < \infty$.

The $\chi_k$ also decrease to the Bernstein index $\nu = \inf_k \chi_k$ at every point.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax606786.Cocycles
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic

/-!
---
title: The Lyapunov exponents are limits, forwards, backwards and over balanced intervals
type: theorem
---
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$ with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and
$k \ge 1$. Then $\chi_k$ is measurable, and for almost every $\omega$ the $\limsup$ defining it is a
limit, along forward orbits, along backward orbits and over balanced intervals:
$$\chi_k(\omega) = \lim_n \tfrac1n \log \rho_k(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega)
  = \lim_n \tfrac1n \log \rho_k(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_{\sigma^{-n}\omega})
  = \lim_n \tfrac1{2n} \log \rho_k(\mathcal{L}^{(2n)}_{\sigma^{-n}\omega}).$$
Moreover $\chi_1 \ge \chi_2 \ge \cdots$ pointwise, $\nu \le \chi_k$, and almost everywhere
$\chi_1 \le \int \log^+ \|\mathcal{L}\| \, d\mu < \infty$.

The $\chi_k$ also decrease to the Bernstein index $\nu = \inf_k \chi_k$ at every point.
-/

namespace Lax606786.ExponentLimits

open MeasureTheory Filter Topology TopologicalSpace
open Lax606786.Cocycles Lax606786.OperatorStatistics Lax606786.ExtendedLog

variable {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
  [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X]

/-- `χ_k` is measurable. -/
axiom measurable_chi (R : Cocycle Ω X) [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] :
    Measurable (R.chi k)

/-- `χ_k` is an a.e. limit along forward orbits. -/
axiom ae_tendsto_chi (R : Cocycle Ω X) [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
      logEReal (bernsteinNumber (R.iterate n ω) k) / (n : EReal)) atTop (𝓝 (R.chi k ω))

/-- `χ_k` is an a.e. limit along backward orbits. -/
axiom ae_tendsto_chi_backward (R : Cocycle Ω X) [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (k : ℕ)
    [NeZero k] :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
      logEReal (bernsteinNumber (R.iterate n ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω)) k) / (n : EReal))
      atTop (𝓝 (R.chi k ω))

/-- `χ_k` is an a.e. limit over the balanced intervals `[-n, n)`. -/
axiom ae_tendsto_chi_balanced (R : Cocycle Ω X) [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (k : ℕ)
    [NeZero k] :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => logEReal
      (bernsteinNumber (R.iterate (2 * n) ((R.σ.symm : Ω → Ω)^[n] ω)) k) /
        ((2 * n : ℕ) : EReal))
      atTop (𝓝 (R.chi k ω))

/-- `χ_1 ≥ χ_2 ≥ ⋯`. -/
axiom chi_antitone (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) : Antitone fun k : ℕ => R.chi (k + 1) ω

/-- `ν ≤ χ_k` for `k ≥ 1`. -/
axiom nu_le_chi (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) : R.nu ω ≤ R.chi k ω

/-- `χ_1 < ∞` a.e. -/
axiom ae_chi_one_lt_top (R : Cocycle Ω X) [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.chi 1 ω < ⊤

/-- `χ_1 ≤ ∫ log⁺‖𝓛‖` a.e. -/
axiom ae_chi_one_le_integral (R : Cocycle Ω X) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.chi 1 ω ≤ ((∫ ω, Real.log (max ‖R.L ω‖ 1) ∂(R.μ) : ℝ) : EReal)

/-- The `χ_k` decrease to `ν`. -/
axiom tendsto_chi_nu (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) :
    Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => R.chi (k + 1) ω) atTop (𝓝 (R.nu ω))

end Lax606786.ExponentLimits

  [inst_2 : NormedAddCommGroup X] [inst_3 : NormedSpace Real X] [inst_4 : MeasurableSpace X]
  (R : Lax606786.Cocycles.Cocycle Ω X),
  Filter.Eventually
    (fun ω =>
      instPartialOrderEReal.le (R.chi 1 ω)
        (MeasureTheory.integral R.μ fun ω =>
            Real.log (Real.instMax.max (ContinuousLinearMap.hasOpNorm.norm (R.L ω)) 1)).toEReal)

concepts.title: The logarithm with values in the extended reals
concepts.description:
For $r \ge 0$ the logarithm $\log r \in [-\infty, \infty)$, with $\log 0 = -\infty$. Growth rates

/-!
---
title: The logarithm with values in the extended reals
type: definition
---
For $r \ge 0$ the logarithm $\log r \in [-\infty, \infty)$, with $\log 0 = -\infty$. Growth rates
$\lim \frac1n \log a_n$ are taken with this logarithm, so that a sequence which vanishes has rate
$-\infty$. (Arguments $r < 0$ do not occur; they are also sent to $-\infty$.)
-/

namespace Lax606786.ExtendedLog

/-- `log r` for `r > 0`, and `-∞` for `r ≤ 0`. -/
noncomputable def logEReal (r : ℝ) : EReal := if r ≤ 0 then ⊥ else (Real.log r : EReal)

end Lax606786.ExtendedLog

concepts.title: Unit vectors far from a subspace of smaller dimension
concepts.description:
Let $X$ be a real normed space and $A, W \le X$ finite-dimensional subspaces with
$\dim W < \dim A$. Then there is a unit vector $u \in A$ with
$$d(u, W) \ge \frac{1}{1 + \dim W}.$$

import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

/-!
---
title: Unit vectors far from a subspace of smaller dimension
type: theorem
---
Let $X$ be a real normed space and $A, W \le X$ finite-dimensional subspaces with
$\dim W < \dim A$. Then there is a unit vector $u \in A$ with
$$d(u, W) \ge \frac{1}{1 + \dim W}.$$
-/

namespace Lax606786.FarUnitVectors

/-- A unit vector of `A` at distance at least `1 / (1 + dim W)` from `W`. -/
axiom exists_unit_far_of_finrank_lt {X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]
    {A W : Submodule ℝ X} [FiniteDimensional ℝ A] [FiniteDimensional ℝ W]
    (h : Module.finrank ℝ W < Module.finrank ℝ A) :
    ∃ u ∈ A, ‖u‖ = 1 ∧ (1 : ℝ) / (1 + Module.finrank ℝ W) ≤ Metric.infDist u (W : Set X)

end Lax606786.FarUnitVectors

concepts.title: Fast spaces
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on $X$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$. A family
$E \colon \Omega \to \mathcal{G}_k X$ of $k$-dimensional subspaces is a *fast space* of
multiplicity $k$ at rate $\lambda$ when it is measurable and equivariant
($\mathcal{L}_\omega E(\omega) = E(\sigma\omega)$ almost surely), and almost surely every nonzero
vector of $E(\omega)$ has growth rate $\lambda$ and
$\tfrac1n \log g(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega, E(\omega)) \to \lambda$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax606786.Cocycles
import Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian
import Lax606786.ExtendedLog

/-!
---
title: Fast spaces
type: definition
---
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on $X$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$. A family
$E \colon \Omega \to \mathcal{G}_k X$ of $k$-dimensional subspaces is a *fast space* of
multiplicity $k$ at rate $\lambda$ when it is measurable and equivariant
($\mathcal{L}_\omega E(\omega) = E(\sigma\omega)$ almost surely), and almost surely every nonzero
vector of $E(\omega)$ has growth rate $\lambda$ and
$\tfrac1n \log g(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega, E(\omega)) \to \lambda$.
-/

namespace Lax606786.FastSpaces

open MeasureTheory Filter
open Lax606786.Cocycles Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian Lax606786.OperatorStatistics
  Lax606786.ExtendedLog

/-- `E` is a fast space of multiplicity `k` at rate `lam`. -/
def IsFastSpace {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
    [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X]
    (R : Cocycle Ω X) (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] (lam : ℝ) (E : Ω → GrassmannianFin X k) : Prop :=
  Measurable E ∧
  (∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), ∀ x ∈ (E ω).1, x ≠ 0 → R.lambdaAt ω x = (lam : EReal)) ∧
  (∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), (E ω).1.map (R.L ω : X →ₗ[ℝ] X) = (E (R.σ ω)).1) ∧
  (∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => logEReal (growth (R.iterate n ω) (E ω).1) / (n : EReal))
    atTop (nhds (lam : EReal)))

end Lax606786.FastSpaces

concepts.title: Uniqueness of the fast spaces
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, with
distinct exponents almost surely equal to $\lambda_i$, and let $i \ge 1$. Let $E, E'$ be measurable
equivariant families of subspaces of dimensions almost surely equal to $m_i \ge 1$, both growing at
rate $\lambda_i$ in norm and in slowest growth. Then $E(\omega) = E'(\omega)$ almost surely.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax606786.Cocycles
import Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian

/-!
---
title: Uniqueness of the fast spaces
type: theorem
---
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, with
distinct exponents almost surely equal to $\lambda_i$, and let $i \ge 1$. Let $E, E'$ be measurable
equivariant families of subspaces of dimensions almost surely equal to $m_i \ge 1$, both growing at
rate $\lambda_i$ in norm and in slowest growth. Then $E(\omega) = E'(\omega)$ almost surely.
-/

namespace Lax606786.FastSpaceUniqueness

open MeasureTheory Filter Topology TopologicalSpace
open Lax606786.Cocycles Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian Lax606786.OperatorStatistics
  Lax606786.ExtendedLog

/-- Two fast families at the same exponent and multiplicity agree almost surely. -/
axiom fast_space_unique {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
    [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X]
    (R : Cocycle Ω X) [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
    [CompleteSpace X] {lam : ℕ → EReal} (hlam : ∀ i, ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.lambda i ω = lam i)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) {m m' : ℕ} [NeZero m] [NeZero m']
    (hm : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.mult i ω = m) (hm' : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.mult i ω = m')
    (E : Ω → GrassmannianFin X m) (E' : Ω → GrassmannianFin X m')
    (hEm : Measurable E) (hE'm : Measurable E')
    (hEeq : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), Submodule.map (R.L ω : X →ₗ[ℝ] X) ((E ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)
        = ((E (R.σ ω)).1 : Submodule ℝ X))
    (hE'eq : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), Submodule.map (R.L ω : X →ₗ[ℝ] X) ((E' ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)
        = ((E' (R.σ ω)).1 : Submodule ℝ X))
    (hEn : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => logEReal
        ‖(R.iterate n ω).comp (((E ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)).subtypeL‖ / (n : EReal)) atTop
        (𝓝 (lam i)))
    (hE'n : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => logEReal
        ‖(R.iterate n ω).comp (((E' ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)).subtypeL‖ / (n : EReal)) atTop
        (𝓝 (lam i)))
    (hEg : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => logEReal
        (growth (R.iterate n ω) ((E ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)) / (n : EReal)) atTop (𝓝 (lam i)))
    (hE'g : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => logEReal
        (growth (R.iterate n ω) ((E' ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)) / (n : EReal)) atTop
        (𝓝 (lam i))) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), ((E ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X) = ((E' ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)

end Lax606786.FastSpaceUniqueness

concepts.title: Uniqueness of fast families below a spectral gap
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$ with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and
suppose $\chi_{m+1} < b < a$ almost surely. Two measurable equivariant families
$E, E' \colon \Omega \to \mathcal{G}_m X$ on which $\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega$ eventually grows
faster than $e^{an}$ agree almost everywhere.

This generalises the uniqueness clause of Lemma 28 of Lee (2024).

import Lax606786.Cocycles
import Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian

/-!
---
title: Uniqueness of fast families below a spectral gap
type: theorem
---
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$ with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and
suppose $\chi_{m+1} < b < a$ almost surely. Two measurable equivariant families
$E, E' \colon \Omega \to \mathcal{G}_m X$ on which $\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega$ eventually grows
faster than $e^{an}$ agree almost everywhere.

This generalises the uniqueness clause of Lemma 28 of Lee (2024).
-/

namespace Lax606786.GapUniqueness

open MeasureTheory Filter TopologicalSpace
open Lax606786.Cocycles Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

variable {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
  [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X]

/-- Two equivariant families growing faster than `e^{an}`, with `a` above `χ_{m+1}`, agree. -/
axiom ae_eq_of_fast (R : Cocycle Ω X) [SeparableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
    (m : ℕ) [NeZero m] {a b : ℝ} (hab : b < a)
    (hchi2 : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.chi (m + 1) ω < (b : EReal))
    (E E' : Ω → GrassmannianFin X m) (hEm : Measurable E) (hE'm : Measurable E')
    (hEeq : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), Submodule.map (R.L ω : X →ₗ[ℝ] X) ((E ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)
        = ((E (R.σ ω)).1 : Submodule ℝ X))
    (hE'eq : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), Submodule.map (R.L ω : X →ₗ[ℝ] X) ((E' ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)
        = ((E' (R.σ ω)).1 : Submodule ℝ X))
    (hEfast : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        Real.exp (a * n) < growth (R.iterate n ω) ((E ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X))
    (hE'fast : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        Real.exp (a * n) < growth (R.iterate n ω) ((E' ω).1 : Submodule ℝ X)) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), E ω = E' ω

end Lax606786.GapUniqueness

concepts.title: Gelfand numbers, Bernstein numbers and the compactness seminorm
concepts.description:
Let $X$ be a real normed space, $T$ a bounded operator on $X$ and $k \ge 1$. Then
$$\rho_k(T) \le s_k(T) \le 4^{k-1}(k-1)!\,\rho_k(T) \qquad \text{and} \qquad
  \|T\|_c \le 2k\, s_k(T).$$
The first inequality holds for every $k$. These are Lemmas 31–33 of Lee (2024). Sharper constants
follow from the Kadec–Snobar theorem (Kadec and Snobar 1971; see also Wojtaszczyk 1991, III.B.10) and from
Pietsch's theory of $s$-numbers (Pietsch 1974); any constant depending on $k$ alone suffices for
comparing exponential growth rates.

Gelfand numbers are nonnegative.

import Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

/-!
---
title: Gelfand numbers, Bernstein numbers and the compactness seminorm
type: theorem
---
Let $X$ be a real normed space, $T$ a bounded operator on $X$ and $k \ge 1$. Then
$$\rho_k(T) \le s_k(T) \le 4^{k-1}(k-1)!\,\rho_k(T) \qquad \text{and} \qquad
  \|T\|_c \le 2k\, s_k(T).$$
The first inequality holds for every $k$. These are Lemmas 31–33 of Lee (2024). Sharper constants
follow from the Kadec–Snobar theorem (Kadec and Snobar 1971; see also Wojtaszczyk 1991, III.B.10) and from
Pietsch's theory of $s$-numbers (Pietsch 1974); any constant depending on $k$ alone suffices for
comparing exponential growth rates.

Gelfand numbers are nonnegative.
-/

namespace Lax606786.GelfandBernsteinComparison

open Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

variable {X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]

/-- `ρ_k ≤ s_k`. -/
axiom bernsteinNumber_le_gelfandNumber (T : X →L[ℝ] X) (k : ℕ) :
    bernsteinNumber T k ≤ gelfandNumber T k

/-- `s_k ≤ 4^{k-1} (k-1)! ρ_k`. -/

    gelfandNumber T k ≤ 4 ^ (k - 1) * (Nat.factorial (k - 1) : ℝ) * bernsteinNumber T k

/-- `‖T‖_c ≤ 2k s_k`. -/
axiom compactSeminorm_le_gelfandNumber (T : X →L[ℝ] X) {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    compactSeminorm T ≤ 2 * (k : ℝ) * gelfandNumber T k

/-- Gelfand numbers are nonnegative. -/
axiom gelfandNumber_nonneg (T : X →L[ℝ] X) (k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ gelfandNumber T k

end Lax606786.GelfandBernsteinComparison

concepts.title: The codimension-k Grassmannian as the closed part of the algebraic Grassmannian
concepts.description:
Let $X$ be a real normed space and $k \ge 0$. Mathlib's Grassmannian $G(k, X; \mathbb{R})$ is the
algebro-geometric one: over the field $\mathbb{R}$ its points are the subspaces $N \le X$ of
codimension $k$, closed or not. The Grassmannian $\mathcal{G}^k X$ of the concept
`BanachGrassmannian` consists of the closed subspaces of codimension $k$, each of which admits a
bounded projection, and carries a metric. The map $V \mapsto V$ identifies $\mathcal{G}^k X$ with
the subspaces in $G(k, X; \mathbb{R})$ that are closed in $X$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Grassmannian

/-!
---
title: The codimension-k Grassmannian as the closed part of the algebraic Grassmannian
type: theorem
---
Let $X$ be a real normed space and $k \ge 0$. Mathlib's Grassmannian $G(k, X; \mathbb{R})$ is the
algebro-geometric one: over the field $\mathbb{R}$ its points are the subspaces $N \le X$ of
codimension $k$, closed or not. The Grassmannian $\mathcal{G}^k X$ of the concept
`BanachGrassmannian` consists of the closed subspaces of codimension $k$, each of which admits a
bounded projection, and carries a metric. The map $V \mapsto V$ identifies $\mathcal{G}^k X$ with
the subspaces in $G(k, X; \mathbb{R})$ that are closed in $X$.
-/

open Module.Grassmannian Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian

/-- `𝒢^k X` is the set of closed points of the algebraic Grassmannian `G(k, X; ℝ)`, by a
bijection that keeps the underlying subspace. -/
axiom exists_equiv_closed (X : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ e : GrassmannianCofin X k ≃
        {N : G(k, X; ℝ) // IsClosed ((N : Submodule ℝ X) : Set X)},
      ∀ V : GrassmannianCofin X k, ((e V).1 : Submodule ℝ X) = V.1.1

end Lax606786.GrassmannianComparison

concepts.title: The Grassmannian contraction estimate
concepts.description:
Let $X$ be a real normed space, $k \ge 1$, $T$ a bounded operator on $X$ and $\Theta$ with
$\rho_{k+1}(T) < \Theta < \rho_k(T)$. Let $V, W \in \mathcal{G}_k X$ with $g(T, V) > \Theta$ and
$g(T, W) > \Theta$. Then $TV, TW \in \mathcal{G}_k X$ and, writing
$x = \rho_{k+1}(T)/\Theta \in [0, 1)$,
$$d(TV, TW) \le \frac{4x}{1-x}.$$
So an operator with a gap between $\rho_{k+1}$ and $\rho_k$ contracts the subspaces on which it
grows fast (Lee 2024, Lemma 12).

import Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

/-!
---
title: The Grassmannian contraction estimate
type: theorem
---
Let $X$ be a real normed space, $k \ge 1$, $T$ a bounded operator on $X$ and $\Theta$ with
$\rho_{k+1}(T) < \Theta < \rho_k(T)$. Let $V, W \in \mathcal{G}_k X$ with $g(T, V) > \Theta$ and
$g(T, W) > \Theta$. Then $TV, TW \in \mathcal{G}_k X$ and, writing
$x = \rho_{k+1}(T)/\Theta \in [0, 1)$,
$$d(TV, TW) \le \frac{4x}{1-x}.$$
So an operator with a gap between $\rho_{k+1}$ and $\rho_k$ contracts the subspaces on which it
grows fast (Lee 2024, Lemma 12).
-/

namespace Lax606786.GrassmannianContraction

open Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

/-- The images of two fast-growing `k`-dimensional subspaces are close. -/
axiom dist_image_le {X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]
    (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] (T : X →L[ℝ] X) (Θ : ℝ)
    (hΘ : bernsteinNumber T (k + 1) < Θ) (hΘ' : Θ < bernsteinNumber T k)
    (V W : GrassmannianFin X k)
    (hV : Θ < growth T (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) (hW : Θ < growth T (W.1 : Submodule ℝ X))
    (TV TW : GrassmannianFin X k)
    (hTV : (TV.1 : Submodule ℝ X) = (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X).map (T : X →ₗ[ℝ] X))
    (hTW : (TW.1 : Submodule ℝ X) = (W.1 : Submodule ℝ X).map (T : X →ₗ[ℝ] X)) :
    dist TV TW ≤ 4 * (bernsteinNumber T (k + 1) / Θ) / (1 - bernsteinNumber T (k + 1) / Θ)

end Lax606786.GrassmannianContraction

concepts.title: The Grassmannian of k-dimensional subspaces is Polish
concepts.description:
Let $X$ be a real normed space and $k \ge 1$, and give $\mathcal{G}_k X$ the Hausdorff distance
between unit spheres. If $X$ is complete then so is $\mathcal{G}_k X$, and if $X$ is separable
then so is $\mathcal{G}_k X$. In particular $\mathcal{G}_k X$ is Polish when $X$ is a separable
Banach space. Completeness of spaces of closed subspaces under the gap distance is classical
(Kato 2013, Chapter IV, §2.1).

concepts.title: Elementary properties of the growth function
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

/-!
---
title: Elementary properties of the growth function
type: theorem
---
Let $X, Y, Z$ be real normed spaces, $T : X \to Y$ and $S : Y \to Z$ bounded operators and
$V \le X$ a subspace. Then

- $0 \le g(T, V) \le \|T\|$, and $g(T, V)\,\|x\| \le \|Tx\|$ for every $x \in V$;
- $g(T, V) \le g(T, W)$ whenever $0 \ne W \le V$;
- $g(T, \operatorname{span}\{u\}) = \|Tu\|$ for every unit vector $u$ (for $T : X \to X$);
- (the growth inequality)
  $$g(T, V)\, g(S, TV) \le g(ST, V) \le \min\bigl(\|T\|\, g(S, TV),\ g(T, V)\,\|S\|\bigr).$$
-/

namespace Lax606786.GrowthFunctionProperties

open Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

variable {X Y Z : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace ℝ Y] [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [NormedSpace ℝ Z]

/-- `g(T, V) ≥ 0`. -/
axiom growth_nonneg (T : X →L[ℝ] Y) (V : Submodule ℝ X) : 0 ≤ growth T V

/-- `g(T, V) ≤ ‖T‖`. -/
axiom growth_le_opNorm (T : X →L[ℝ] Y) (V : Submodule ℝ X) : growth T V ≤ ‖T‖

/-- `g(T, V) ‖u‖ ≤ ‖T u‖` for `u ∈ V`. -/
axiom growth_mul_norm_le (T : X →L[ℝ] Y) {V : Submodule ℝ X} {u : X} (hu : u ∈ V) :
    growth T V * ‖u‖ ≤ ‖T u‖

/-- Shrinking the subspace can only increase the slowest growth. -/
axiom growth_le_growth {T : X →L[ℝ] X} {W V : Submodule ℝ X} (hWV : W ≤ V) (hW : W ≠ ⊥) :
    growth T V ≤ growth T W

/-- The growth on a line is the growth of its unit vector. -/
axiom growth_span_singleton (T : X →L[ℝ] X) {u : X} (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) :
    growth T (Submodule.span ℝ {u}) = ‖T u‖

/-- The growth inequality for a composition. -/
axiom growth_comp_bounds (T : X →L[ℝ] Y) (S : Y →L[ℝ] Z) (V : Submodule ℝ X) :
    growth T V * growth S (V.map (T : X →ₗ[ℝ] Y)) ≤ growth (S.comp T) V ∧
    growth (S.comp T) V ≤ min (‖T‖ * growth S (V.map (T : X →ₗ[ℝ] Y))) (growth T V * ‖S‖)

end Lax606786.GrowthFunctionProperties

concepts.title: Bernstein numbers under a projection
concepts.description:
Let $X$ be a real normed space and $T$ a bounded operator on $X$.

- (Small growth.) If $V \in \mathcal{G}^k X$, $P$ is a bounded projection onto $V$ and
  $l \ge 1$, then $\rho_{k+l}(T) \le \rho_l(TP)$.
- (Large growth.) If $V, V' \in \mathcal{G}^k X$, $P, P'$ are bounded projections onto $V, V'$,
  $E = \ker P$, $P'T = TP$, and $g(T, E) > \|T|_V\|$, then for every $l$,
  $$\rho_l(TP) \le 4\,\|P\|\,\|P'\|\,\rho_{l+k}(T).$$

These are Lemmas 16 and 17 of Lee (2024).

import Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

/-!
---
title: Bernstein numbers under a projection
type: theorem
---
Let $X$ be a real normed space and $T$ a bounded operator on $X$.

- (Small growth.) If $V \in \mathcal{G}^k X$, $P$ is a bounded projection onto $V$ and
  $l \ge 1$, then $\rho_{k+l}(T) \le \rho_l(TP)$.
- (Large growth.) If $V, V' \in \mathcal{G}^k X$, $P, P'$ are bounded projections onto $V, V'$,
  $E = \ker P$, $P'T = TP$, and $g(T, E) > \|T|_V\|$, then for every $l$,
  $$\rho_l(TP) \le 4\,\|P\|\,\|P'\|\,\rho_{l+k}(T).$$

These are Lemmas 16 and 17 of Lee (2024).
-/

namespace Lax606786.GrowthUnderProjections

open Lax606786.BanachGrassmannian Lax606786.OperatorStatistics

variable {X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]

/-- Compressing to a codimension-`k` subspace costs at most `k` Bernstein indices. -/
axiom bernsteinNumber_add_le_comp_proj (k l : ℕ) (hl : l ≠ 0) (V : GrassmannianCofin X k)
    (P : X →L[ℝ] X) (hP : ∀ x, P x ∈ (V.1.1 : Submodule ℝ X))
    (hidem : ∀ x ∈ (V.1.1 : Submodule ℝ X), P x = x) (T : X →L[ℝ] X) :
    bernsteinNumber T (k + l) ≤ bernsteinNumber (T.comp P) l

/-- When `T` grows faster on `ker P` than on `range P`, compressing to `range P` loses at most
`k` Bernstein indices, up to the factor `4 ‖P‖ ‖P'‖`. -/
axiom bernsteinNumber_comp_proj_le (k l : ℕ) (V V' : GrassmannianCofin X k) (E : Submodule ℝ X)
    (P P' T : X →L[ℝ] X)
    (hPproj : LinearMap.IsProj (V.1.1 : Submodule ℝ X) (P : X →ₗ[ℝ] X))
    (hPker : LinearMap.ker (P : X →ₗ[ℝ] X) = E)
    (hP'proj : LinearMap.IsProj (V'.1.1 : Submodule ℝ X) (P' : X →ₗ[ℝ] X))
    (hPcompat : P'.comp T = T.comp P)
    (hfast : growth T E > ‖T.comp (V.1.1 : Submodule ℝ X).subtypeL‖) :
    bernsteinNumber (T.comp P) l ≤ 4 * ‖P‖ * ‖P'‖ * bernsteinNumber T (l + k)

end Lax606786.GrowthUnderProjections

concepts.title: The Bernstein index is the index of compactness
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$. The growth rate of the
compactness seminorm (the distance to the compact operators) of the iterates exists almost
everywhere and equals the Bernstein index $\nu = \lim_k \chi_k$:
$$\lim_n \tfrac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|_c = \nu \quad \text{for a.e. } \omega.$$
Since $\nu$ is almost everywhere constant, the *index of compactness* $\kappa = \lim_n \tfrac1n \log
\|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|_c \in [-\infty, \infty)$ always exists as an almost-everywhere
constant, and $\nu = \kappa$ almost everywhere. This is Lemma 34 of Lee (2024), which assumes that
the limit exists; here its existence is part of the statement.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax606786.Cocycles

/-!
---
title: The Bernstein index is the index of compactness
type: theorem
---
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a cocycle on a separable Banach space $X$. The growth rate of the
compactness seminorm (the distance to the compact operators) of the iterates exists almost
everywhere and equals the Bernstein index $\nu = \lim_k \chi_k$:
$$\lim_n \tfrac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|_c = \nu \quad \text{for a.e. } \omega.$$
Since $\nu$ is almost everywhere constant, the *index of compactness* $\kappa = \lim_n \tfrac1n \log
\|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|_c \in [-\infty, \infty)$ always exists as an almost-everywhere
constant, and $\nu = \kappa$ almost everywhere. This is Lemma 34 of Lee (2024), which assumes that
the limit exists; here its existence is part of the statement.
-/

concepts.title: Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem
concepts.description:
Let $\sigma$ be an ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a probability space
$(\Omega, \mu)$ and $(f_n)$ a subadditive family over $\sigma$ with $f_1^+$ integrable. Let $L_\mu$
denote the lower integral. Then there is a constant $C \in [-\infty, \infty)$ with
$$C = \lim_n L_\mu(f_n/n) = \inf_{n \ge 1} L_\mu(f_n/n)$$
such that $\tfrac1n f_n(\omega) \to C$ for $\mu$-a.e. $\omega$. Limits are taken in the extended
reals. When the $f_n$ are integrable, $L_\mu(f_n/n) = \tfrac1n \int f_n \, d\mu$.

The theorem is due to Kingman (1968); the proof follows Steele (1989).
